title: Trevor Ariza Compares Chris Paul to Power's Ghost
htmlContent:
Former NBA veteran Trevor Arizahas seen just about everything over 18 seasons in the league, but when he was asked to sum up Chris Paul, he didn't reach for a basketball comparison. He reached for television. Appearing on the Out The Mud Podcast with Grizzlies legends Tony Allen and Zach Randolph, Ariza compared the future Hall of Fame point guard to James "Ghost" St. Patrick, the calculating lead character of the Starz drama Power.

"He Like Ghost to Me"

Ariza admitted the comparison might sound a little off at first, but he stood by it.

"He like Ghost to me," Ariza said, before explaining exactly what he meant.

For Ariza, the connection comes down to two sides of the same personality. On the court, he described Paul as the same kind of gritty operator Ghost is in the show, someone who refuses to back down and finds a way to win the moment in front of him. Off the court, it's the business mind. Ghost, played by Omari Hardwick, spent the series balancing a polished public life as a nightclub owner with a ruthless, strategic approach to everything he touched. Ariza sees that same professionalism and calculation in how Paul has handled his career away from the hardwood.

"I feel like if there was a character to describe, bro, Ghost... in the terms of basketball."

Ariza Speaks From Experience

Ariza isn't offering an outsider's take. He shared a locker room with Paul twice: first in New Orleans with the Hornets, where Ariza arrived in 2010 during Paul's final season with the franchise, and again in Houston, where the two teamed with James Harden on the 2017–18 Rockets.

Ariza knows what a winning culture looks like. The 6-foot-8 wing out of UCLA was a second-round pick, No. 43 overall by the New York Knicks in 2004, and turned that long-shot start into an 18-year career across 10 franchises. He played all 82 games for the 2008–09 Los Angeles Lakers and won a championship that season. Over 1,118 regular-season games, he averaged 10.4 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals while building a reputation as one of the league's most reliable 3-and-D wings, with a career high of 40 points in a single game.

That background matters. Ariza was the type of player who did the dirty work, guarding the best perimeter scorer every night. When a player like that calls someone gritty, it carries weight.

Chris Paul's Résumé Backs It Up

Paul, who retired in February 2026 after 21 NBA seasons, built a career that fits Ariza's description on both fronts. The No. 4 overall pick out of Wake Forest in 2005 won Rookie of the Year, earned 12 All-Star selections and 11 All-NBA nods, and finished No. 2 all-time in both assists (12,552) and steals (2,728).

The grit shows up most clearly on defense. Paul made nine All-Defensive teams, seven of them First Team, and led the league in steals six times — a league record. For a 6-foot point guard, that level of defensive production speaks to the competitive edge Ariza highlighted.

The business side is just as real. Paul played for seven franchises, including two stints with the Clippers, and spent years as president of the National Basketball Players Association. He was known for running teams like a CEO, demanding precision from teammates and coaches alike.

The Missing Piece

There is one more parallel, even if Ariza didn't say it outright. Ghost spent all of Power chasing a legitimate empire that always seemed just out of reach. Paul's career has a similar storyline. Despite two Olympic gold medals, a spot on the NBA 75th Anniversary Team and a first-ballot Hall of Fame case, he never won an NBA championship.

The closest he came may have been that 2017–18 Houston team with Ariza, which pushed the Golden State Warriors to seven games in the Western Conference Finals before Paul's hamstring injury changed the series.

A Comparison That Sticks

Basketball players get compared to other players all the time. Ariza's take stands out because it captures something statistics alone don't: the mix of toughness, control and calculation that defined Paul for two decades. Coming from a former teammate and champion, on a show hosted by two of the grittiest players of their era in Allen and Randolph, the Ghost comparison feels less like a joke and more like an honest scouting report.
excerpt: Former NBA veteran Trevor Ariza appeared on the Out The Mud Podcast with Tony Allen and Zach Randolph and compared 21-season point guard Chris Paul to James "Ghost" St. Patrick from the Starz drama Power, citing Paul's rare blend of on-court grit and off-court calculation.
